match.seen: From 0 to 17 s the board is clearly a plus-shaped grid with the corners cut away, and every block is orange or blue. I count about 8 blocks at 0 s.
The clock reaches zero at 17 s with one orange T-shaped block still on the board. The replay at 24 to 25 s and the Out of Time screen at 26 to 28 s confirm it.
The ad is exactly 35 s long. Blocks are cleared at a steady rate from 1 to 15 s, but the replay from 18 to 25 s plays the same final seconds again and slows things down.

The captions are dark navy or purple, as asked. Behind the board, the gameplay from 0 to 25 s sits on a pale icy blue rather than mint, with little fade toward white. Only the end card from 29 to 34 s shows a real mint-to-white fade.
The tool used its standard captions: "Can you beat the clock?" (0 to 1 s), "Oops!" (3 to 4 s), "Hurry!" (13 to 15 s) and "So close!" (26 to 28 s).
Gameplay runs to 17 s, the replay from 18 to 25 s, Out of Time from 26 to 28 s, then the end card from 29 to 34 s.
Only the game's own board, blocks, timer and end-card stopwatch appear. No outside pictures are used.
This is a new ad, so there was nothing to keep.

review.why: Racing the clock on a neat cross-shaped board looks fun and the near miss teases me, but the long replay of the last few seconds made me want to scroll on.
fixes: Change the background behind the gameplay to a clear mint green that fades to white at the bottom, so it matches the end card and the brief.
Cut the slow-motion replay to about 3 seconds and give the time to the live play, so the ad keeps moving.
Make the captions bigger and bolder with a light outline, so the small dark text stands out on the board.
review.suggested_edit: Keep everything, but change the background behind the board during gameplay and the replay to a clear mint green that fades to white at the bottom, matching the end card.
